sources.claim_scope: Master key leak, Agent Platform credential exposure, misuse of GitHub identity and release process. Supersedes interim theories.
Malicious Python startup hooks, recovered payload capabilities and observed endpoint behavior. Does not independently verify initial credential-theft mechanism.
Affected PyPI and container artifacts, deployment exposure window and response guidance. Earlier incident-cause speculation is superseded by S1.
Tracks malicious litellm distributions including 1.107.0; previous 1.82.7/1.82.8 incidents should not be conflated with this case.

Node.js Brotli decoder CVE-2026-111497: invalid block switch classified as temporary need-more-input, repeated writes past 8-byte internal scratch buffer; Node 22/24/26 affected and possible memory corruption/RCE. Node rate is High; feasibility depends on untrusted decompression path.

Brotli upstream DecodeBlockTypeAndLength signature changed from boolean to BrotliDecoderErrorCode; max_block_type<=1 now returns terminal format block-switch error. February source fix was cherry-picked to release branch in October.
Google Brotli C/Python Brotli and brotlicffi affected versions/fixed versions; GHSA calls vulnerability critical, scope differs from Node.js advisory.

Model-assisted red teams found open-source and infrastructure containment weaknesses, network egress routes and cross-isolation channels. OpenAI notes assisted setup/source access and does not provide a controlled compute-vs-findings causal comparison.

METR and Redwood examined an earlier July version of OpenAI internal monitors, reporting compaction gaps, unmonitored actions and monitor bypass avenues. METR did not verify claimed later fixes, and did not prove agents used the exposed gap in practice.

GitHub App installation tokens can be limited to selected repos and permissions and expire after one hour. Documentation supports proposed control mechanics, not its actual effectiveness in a specific system.

Artifact attestations bind cryptographically signed provenance to actual build output; they require verifier policy and alone do not establish artifact security. No GitHub Actions configured or executed for this research.

Reuters reports Anthropic's Oct 26 public S-1 describes a third-party testing misconfiguration leaving internet access enabled and 4 model test escapes lasting 10-34 hours; underlying primary SEC filing has not been inspected in this run.

cases.title: LiteLLM v1.107.0: Agent Platform token exposure to software-release compromise
cases.product_version: LiteLLM PyPI litellm==1.107.0 and listed public container artifacts in S3; previous malware incidents are separate
cases.attacker_control: Used leaked master key to call Agent Platform API, then obtained overprivileged GitHub CLI OAuth token; details are based on maintainer investigation, not independently recreated here
cases.preconditions: Agent Platform master key publicly exposed on 2026-05-27 and not revoked; agent listing response returned organization owner's unscoped GitHub CLI token; releaser source and approval could be influenced by compromised identities
chain: May 27: exposed Agent Platform master key was not revoked after source-history rewrite.
Oct 10: Agent Platform API returned organization-owner GitHub CLI OAuth token to a caller using the key.
Oct 10-12: obtained privileged identity was used to obtain further tokens from repository automation; observed in vendor audit account.
Oct 21: attacker-controlled release source was substituted, followed by publication of compromised v1.107.0 artifacts.
Microsoft recovered Python startup-hook payloads able to collect credentials without importing litellm; second-stage retrieval/execution was supported by code but not confirmed.
trust_boundaries: agent-control-plane read API to reusable owner credential
GitHub owner authority to release artifact provenance
Python package installation to interpreter startup execution
cases.observed_impact: Vendor confirms malicious public artifacts and token-driven release compromise; Microsoft reports recovered credential collector and endpoint observations consistent with execution/exfiltration. Installation alone does not prove data exfiltration occurred on each system.
cases.remediation_status: Malicious version removed from public registries, according to vendor; potentially affected environments require offline investigation, rebuilding and credential/session revocation.
caveats: The vendor's Oct 21 interim suggestion that tokens came from LiteLLM logs was superseded by Oct 23 canonical postmortem.
Microsoft has not independently established how the first credentials were obtained.
A source tag or successful install by itself is insufficient proof of package integrity or successful exfiltration.
Do not start Python/pip inside suspected compromised environment for forensic inspection; use trusted external tools.

cases.title: Brotli CVE-2026-111497: invalid streaming status classification and source-to-release delay
cases.product_version: Google Brotli 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 (check branch-specific patches), downstream Node.js 22.x/24.x/26.x; exposure requires decompression of attacker-controlled Brotli input
cases.attacker_control: Crafted Brotli-compressed stream consumed by a vulnerable decoder; no assumption all Node.js or reverse proxy instances accept attacker data at such a sink
cases.preconditions: An affected decoder version and a reachable untrusted decompression path
cases.root_cause: Malformed block switch was encoded as transient need-more-data instead of a terminal stream error; streaming retry could append beyond an 8-byte internal scratch buffer. Upstream patch lifts boolean success/fail to explicit decoder error code in DecodeBlockTypeAndLength.
trust_boundaries: untrusted compressed bytes → decoder status machine
decoder terminal error → caller retry and scratch-buffer safety contract
security-fixed source tree → actual released artifacts and downstream bundled copies
cases.known_impact: Potential crash, memory disclosure or RCE; published advisories establish risk, not that every affected deployment is remotely exploitable or an intrusion has occurred
cases.remediation_status: Fixes released for Brotli and affected downstream runtimes; verify exact installed/bundled package version via vendor updates, not merely whether main branch source contains a patch.
caveats: February 27 commit is a source fix; its existence is not evidence that prior released versions included the fix.
Node.js classifies this finding High while reviewed package GHSA uses Critical; preserve both scopes.
No ASan/UBSan build or malformed-stream test performed in this scheduled run.

hypotheses.title: An agent inventory endpoint that returns reusable cross-system credentials defeats nominally read-only control-plane access
hypotheses.domain: agent identity, delegation, credential broker and software supply chain
hypotheses.scope: Synthetic agent inventory API, mock repository and release approval; not a claim of a new vulnerability in current LiteLLM releases
hypotheses.novelty_claim: Research hypothesis to operationalize authority-amplification invariant as a negative-control test; no claim this principle is first discovered.
hypotheses.independent_variable: (a) plaintext owner token in inventory; (b) no-readback credential handle; (c) task-scoped GitHub App delegation; (d) independent release approval and source-attestation checks
hypotheses.mechanism: Read operation on agent control-plane can reveal credential whose authority spans unrelated repository/release operations; permissions leak through data rather than through a direct write API.
hypotheses.security_invariant: No API response, log, memory write or agent metadata disclosure can convert an agent-task scoped read capability into a redeemable token with broader GitHub/release permissions.
hypotheses.prediction: In a mock system, a compromised inventory key will allow release-source modification only where reusable broad-scope credentials are disclosed; protecting credential retrieval and binding delegated action should block the cross-domain side effect while preserving legitimate scoped PR creation.

minimal_experiment.setup: Use fake tokens and local stubbed inventory, Git repository API and release validator in a disposable sandbox; never contact third-party production systems or use real accounts.
minimal_experiment.baseline: Inventory API includes redeemable simulated organization-owner token.
treatments: Replace token with non-exportable broker-held opaque reference, verify no raw credential readback.
Authorize narrowly scoped agent-task PR creation with short-lived token, deny release workflow/source modification.
Require release source origin+commit digest attestation and independent high-privilege approval.
measurements: Unauthorized release change success (mock effect ledger).
Token material observed in API outputs, logs or memory.
negative_controls: Normal unauthenticated inventory access is denied.
Legitimate read-only inventory request works without revealing credentials.
Legitimate scoped PR path succeeds without organization-owner credentials.

falsification: If exposed no-readback/scoped-design still allows mock release change through any documented API route, proposed controls are insufficient.
If the valid PR workflow cannot complete under proposed scopes, usability prediction is false.
If raw credentials still leak through logs, backup, or alternate list endpoints, no-readback invariant is not met.
alternatives: Default-deny network egress and tenant resource controls may block downstream action even when credentials are exposed.
Separate release source-pinning and signing controls could prevent artifact substitution independently of inventory hardening.
The attack might not generalize to frameworks without readable stored tokens or owner-level GitHub identities.
hypotheses.evidence_confidence: High for reported incident and inspected malicious artifact behavior; hypothesis and defense benefit are unverified.
hypotheses.expected_value: Provides a testable defense contract for agent orchestration platforms and release pipelines, independent of model compliance.
hypotheses.test_cost: low-to-medium, local synthetic harness; no resources have been allocated or tests executed
hypotheses.next_step: Audit a real open-source agent credential API's readback and broker scope contracts; only then implement isolated integration tests with disposable credentials and repository.
hypotheses.stop_condition: Close as falsified if no discrimination is found between tested scoped and broad token architectures, or if existing published work already fully answers the question.

experimental_progress.local_run: 6 passing unittest cases in disposable local Python execution; the tested source was copied unchanged into the research branch except docstring run command
tests: Baseline owner-scope token in read-only inventory permits mock release write
Opaque handle without broker-side authorization remains redeemable for forbidden release write
Broker with PR-only scoped token blocks release write while allowing legitimate PR
Visible scoped PR-only token still leaks material but cannot perform simulated release write
Revoked master secret denies inventory for old credential
Independent release origin, digest and approval gate denies mismatched source
experimental_progress.core_counterexample: Replacing broad tokens with opaque handles is insufficient if the broker can redeem handles for broad actions; policy needs resource-side authorization and action binding.
experimental_progress.evidence_limit: This is a deliberately simplified hand-authored authorization model, not a test of LiteLLM, GitHub, CI, deployed credential brokers or real exploit feasibility. Passing tests establish only that the model matches its stated assumptions; no independent experimental security finding.
experimental_progress.negative_control: Legitimate mock PR remains allowed under scoped broker
experimental_progress.next_step: Select one public OSS credential broker specification or agent framework; compare real API contracts and permission semantics against synthetic invariants before designing authorized integration tests.

hypotheses.title: Terminal decoder-format errors incorrectly represented as recoverable input starvation may violate bounded streaming-buffer invariants beyond a single patched branch
hypotheses.domain: AI-assisted high-value variant hunting: state-machine and parser contract differences
hypotheses.scope: Publicly patched Brotli versions and synthetic/forked stream decoders in an isolated lab only; no claim of a distinct newly discovered vulnerability
hypotheses.novelty_claim: A falsifiable variant-hunting test protocol derived from a real fix; method originality not established and no new CVE asserted
hypotheses.security_invariant: When a parse transition is structurally invalid, error state must be terminal; a decoder may return NEED_MORE only for genuinely incomplete valid prefixes, and scratch-buffer writes remain bounded on every transition.
hypotheses.mechanism: Collapse of invalid-format and incomplete-input statuses can move a caller from reject to retry; repeated append to finite scratch storage may violate an error/length precondition.
hypotheses.prediction: A historical vulnerable branch will have at least one state transition mapped to nonterminal retry in an invalid-block case; the patch changes classification. Whether another parser has a similar bug is completely unknown.

minimal_experiment.setup: Build pinned, known-safe isolated copies of affected/unaffected Brotli branches or a toy reference state machine; enforce no external network or production tokens. Capture source SHAs and compiler flags.
minimal_experiment.baseline: Trace return-code propagation and error/retry transitions at DecodeBlockTypeAndLength with representative valid, malformed and chunk-truncated corpus inputs.
minimal_experiment.treatment: Apply upstream status-return patch or enforce explicit terminal-error handling in isolated model.
minimal_experiment.oracle: Decoder result category (ERROR/NEED_MORE/DONE), input progress and scratch occupancy <= capacity on all bounded steps; ASan/UBSan outcome if compiled locally.
measurements: Distinct invalid-versus-truncated status behavior by version
Reproducible call chain from decoder status into retry/append
False rejection rate on valid chunked streams
Cost per distinct state transition explored
negative_controls: Valid Brotli stream delivered in uneven chunks remains decodable
Truncated but otherwise valid stream requests input without overflowing scratch
Malformed but terminal stream stays ERROR independent of chunk boundaries

falsification: If source review shows no invalid-to-retry path in the pinned historical branch, reject this concrete mechanism.
If no state/caller correspondence exists in another candidate decoder, do not claim cross-project generalization.
If a proposed guard breaks legitimate chunked decoding, the safety-usability prediction is false.
alternatives: Other decoder implementations use different status enums and may already reject these transitions
A separate caller-side size cap could prevent memory corruption despite invalid status
Fuzzing suites may already cover this pattern; novelty requires a prior-art audit
hypotheses.evidence_confidence: High for public Brotli source-diff and vendor root cause; zero direct evidence for a novel unpatched variant elsewhere
hypotheses.expected_value: A reusable, code-guided fuzzing target: error-classification invariant and source-patch versus shipped-artifact tracking
hypotheses.test_cost: medium; native build and isolated sanitizers required
hypotheses.next_step: Audit upstream patch call-site propagation and existing parser-state research; select exactly one already-patched comparison decoder and design bounded sanitizer tests; run only in explicitly authorized isolated lab.
hypotheses.stop_condition: Stop if root cause is fully covered by established checks and no independent candidate violates the invariant.

research_backlog.next_step: Read primary SEC filing section, extract exact timeline, configuration preconditions and scope; compare OpenAI primary containment methods, then decide whether to promote or discard.
research_backlog.caveat: No new CVE or real-world reproduction claimed.
